source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 111(4), published p.1036 / PDF p.1, abstract and opening: multiple specialized modules expose limited buffer contents to a central rule system; one rule is selected at a time and subsymbolic processes guide selection and module operations

Psychological Review 111(4), published p.1037 / PDF p.2, architecture overview and Figure 1: visual, manual, declarative and goal modules communicate limited information through module-specific buffers to a central rule-selection system

Psychological Review 111(4), published p.1038 / PDF p.3, architecture cycle: module-internal processing can proceed in parallel and asynchronously; buffers expose limited chunks; current buffer patterns are matched, one rule fires, and buffers are updated in an approximately 50-ms serial cycle

Psychological Review 111(4), published p.1044 / PDF p.9, procedural-control section: multiple applicable rules compete under serial execution; utility equals estimated goal-success value minus estimated cost, utilities vary noisily from cycle to cycle, and the currently highest-valued applicable rule is selected

Psychological Review 111(4), published pp.1056-1057 / PDF pp.21-22, General Discussion: the architecture is explicitly incomplete; direct cortical connections can bypass the serial central route, while the proposed integration account remains parallel modules -> buffers -> central pattern detection and coordinated action

conditions: integrated task performance requiring coordination among specialized perceptual, action, goal-maintenance and retrieval subsystems
the architecture's central coordination route has access only to limited interface contents rather than unrestricted subsystem-internal processing
specialized subsystem processing can proceed in parallel and asynchronously, while the central rule-selection step is serial
the source explicitly treats this central integration route as incomplete rather than as the only possible route for all processing; direct subsystem-to-subsystem pathways may bypass it
population: human cognition as modeled by the source architecture
substrate: specialized information-processing subsystems, limited interface states, and a central serial rule-selection loop with proposed cortical and subcortical associations
task: coordinate perception, maintained goals, retrieval and action by matching limited interface contents to applicable condition-action mappings and executing one mapping per central cycle
temporal_scope: parallel and asynchronous subsystem processing is interleaved with repeating serial central cycles of approximately 50 ms in the source's architecture

nodes.description: set of specialized perceptual, action, goal-maintenance and retrieval subsystems whose internal processing is partly encapsulated and can proceed in parallel
limited module-specific interface contents through which selected subsystem information becomes available to central coordination
joint pattern of currently exposed interface contents available to the central matching process
condition-action mappings whose conditions match the current interface pattern
cycle-specific noisy control value for an applicable mapping, based on estimated probability of achieving the current goal, goal value, and estimated cost
single applicable condition-action mapping with the highest currently realized control value on the central cycle
interface-state change or request to a specialized subsystem produced by execution of the selected mapping
source-acknowledged direct connection between processing subsystems that can permit some processing to bypass the serial central coordination route

relations.description: specialized subsystems expose only limited selected information through their interface states to the central coordination route
the current information available to central coordination is constrained to the contents exposed at the subsystem interfaces
which condition-action mappings are applicable depends on the current pattern of exposed interface contents
because central execution is serial, one applicable mapping is selected according to its cycle-specific noisy control value
executing the selected mapping produces interface-state changes or requests to specialized subsystems
within each central cycle, exposed interface contents are matched before one mapping is selected and executed, after which interface contents can be updated for the next cycle
the source distinguishes direct subsystem connections from the buffer-mediated serial coordination route and explicitly notes that not all processing must pass through the latter
